analysis.reading:
TWO TITLES, ONE WORK, ONE DAY, ONE DOI. On 4 August the «rebekah cranes sappho» capture surfaced a Zenodo record titled "ΦΑΙΝΕΤΑΙ ΜΟΙ — Sappho 31 with Reconstructed FOURTH Stanza", and I recorded it as the archive’s own error propagating outward. This capture completes the picture: Hello Poetry carries the SAME WORK, dated the SAME DAY, 2 February 2026, titled Reconstructed FIFTH Stanza. SciLynk carries FIFTH too, with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18459573 — the same DOI as the Zenodo record that says FOURTH.

So the error is not downstream drift and not a later corruption. BOTH FORMS WERE PUBLISHED SIMULTANEOUSLY ACROSS SURFACES, and the wrong one landed on the deposit that carries the DOI. Sappho 31 has five stanzas; the Cranes reconstruction supplies the fifth. Hello Poetry and SciLynk are right; the Zenodo title is wrong; the correction is a metadata fix on one record, not a campaign.

Card 2 is a real scholarly gift and is not the archive’s: OAPEN quoting Campbell on the fragment’s ending — "it is an obvious but UNVERIFIABLE CONJECTURE that it was unsatisfied love" — Schubart, Wilamowitz, Lobel and Page all named. The philological tradition’s own admission that the poem’s close is conjectural, retrieved beside a reconstruction of it.

Polytonic Greek transmits again in card 5, Fragment 1 with breathings, accents and iota subscript intact.
